members.name: Osric Dunn
members.role: headman of Thornby; owes Brackenford's store forty baskets of grain and pays slowly in fish
ties: owes Aldric Marrow's town store forty baskets
thinks Edda at the north light wrecked his brother's boat

members.name: Rona Dunn
members.role: Osric's wife; keeps the village cook-fire and smokes the catch for the common store
ties: trades smoked fish with Simon Hollis

members.name: Perrin Dunn
members.role: Osric's son; fishes the north shore with his father and keeps the boat
ties: owes Simon Hollis for a net

members.name: Inga Dunn
members.role: Osric's niece; fishes the shallows from a small boat and mends the village nets
ties: thinks Edda Wray should be watched

members.name: Hob Dunn
members.role: Perrin's cousin, raised in the Dunn house; mends nets and plays on the shingle

members.name: Cuthbert Stave
members.role: hunts the north shore and the cape for the village; keeps the fish road clear of wolves
ties: grudges Edda Wray for his brother's boat

members.name: Merrow Stave
members.role: Cuthbert's wife; keeps the village's small barley and vegetable plots above the shore
ties: sells barley to Brackenford's store against the debt

members.name: Wren Stave
members.role: Cuthbert and Merrow's daughter; helps in the plots and follows her father to the cape

members.name: Sedge Gannet
members.role: fishes the deep water off the cape from a tarred boat; a quiet man with a sharp eye for weather
ties: sells his catch to Rona Dunn
owes Osric Dunn for a share of a net
blames Edda Wray's light for a near wreck last winter

members.name: Tern Gannet
members.role: carries smoked fish from Thornby down the fish road to Brackenford's market and brings grain back
ties: runs the fish road with Simon Hollis
pays the gate-due at Brackenford and hates it

members.name: Minnow Gannet
members.role: Sedge and Tern's daughter; plays on the shingle and helps her mother pack the fish

members.name: Rook Tarn
members.role: old fisher who no longer goes out; mends nets and keeps the village's tally of the debt to Brackenford
ties: keeps the debt tally for Osric Dunn

members.name: Mavis Tarn
members.role: Rook's wife; keeps the goats and the herb plot behind their house

members.name: Pike Tarn
members.role: Rook and Mavis's son; hunts the cape and the shore for birds and small game
ties: thinks the debt to Brackenford will never be paid

situations.summary: Thornby still owes Brackenford's store forty baskets of grain from the Lean Year; Osric pays in fish and barley as he can, and the ledger in Brackenford records every basket. Rook Tarn keeps the village tally, and the two counts have begun to drift apart.

sides.Osric Dunn: He knows the debt is real and feels it every time he loads fish for Brackenford; he wants it paid but fears the village cannot pay and eat.
sides.Rook Tarn: He keeps the tally and believes Brackenford's ledger has more baskets on it than Thornby ever took; he wants Osric to demand a recount.
sides.Tern Gannet: She carries the payments down the fish road and pays the gate-due on top; she feels the debt as a weight on every trip and resents the due more than the debt.

situations.summary: Thornby blames old Edda Wray at the north light for wrecking boats, and Sedge Gannet's near wreck last winter has hardened the talk. Edda says she lights it every night. No one has gone up to the cape to ask her plainly.

sides.Sedge Gannet: He came close to losing his boat in the dark and is sure the light was wrong; he wants the village to take the light away from her.
sides.Cuthbert Stave: His brother drowned off the cape years ago and he has blamed Edda since; he feels the grudge as a family duty.
sides.Osric Dunn: He thinks Edda wrecked his brother's boat and says so, but he is headman and knows an accusation is not a proof.
sides.Rook Tarn: He grumbles with the rest but remembers Edda's light guiding him home in bad weather; he is not sure.

situations.summary: Perrin Dunn and Inga Dunn are courting; they are cousins by marriage and the village has begun to talk about whether the headman's house should keep it in the family. Rona Dunn has said nothing to either of them.

sides.Perrin Dunn: He wants to marry Inga and take the boat with her; he does not see what the talk is about.
sides.Inga Dunn: She wants Perrin but feels the village's eyes on her; she has not told him what the women say at the smoke shed.
sides.Rona Dunn: She has heard the talk and is uneasy about the match; she keeps her counsel but watches Inga at the cook-fire.
sides.Osric Dunn: He is fond of Inga and has not thought about it at all; he assumes Perrin will do as he likes.

situations.summary: Cuthbert Stave and Pike Tarn both hunt the cape and both claim the best trapping ground above the shore; each has moved the other's snares, and neither will say so to Osric.

sides.Cuthbert Stave: He has hunted the cape since he was a boy and thinks Pike's snares are too close to his line; he moved them and feels justified.
sides.Pike Tarn: He found his snares shifted and knows who did it; he wants the headman to settle the ground but will not be the one to ask.
sides.Osric Dunn: He has heard both men grumble and wants the cape hunt kept quiet; he has not chosen between them.
